findings.title: Recreate-upgrade exit code changed from 4 to 3 (breaking change)
findings.body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE moves from 4 to 3, and 4 is reused for FEATURE_DISABLED. Any script or operator logic that treats 4 as 'recreate required' will now read it as 'feature disabled', and 3 gets a new meaning. The docs were updated, but other consumers of the old code (for example the operator) need to be checked and migrated. The tool is only a preview, which reduces the impact.

findings.title: Docs macro appends the feature flag after user parameters
findings.body: The macro hard-codes `--features=rolling-updates` at the end of every update-compatibility example. This is fine for the docs, but it hides from readers that the flag is a preview requirement. It also suffixes the flag to the whole parameter list, which is awkward if a user already passes `--features`.

findings.title: Feature check runs before config validation and the preview warning
findings.body: When the feature is disabled the command exits with code 4 and never validates the `--file` argument. A user who passes a bad or missing file path therefore gets 'feature not enabled' first, and a pipeline can misread exit 4. This is acceptable, but note the `return` after `picocli.exit(...)`. If `exit` only records the code rather than terminating, the guard still works because of the `return`.
